'''Samuel David Young''' (born June 1, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played four seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), among other leagues worldwide. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]].

==Early years==
The eldest of five children, Young was born  in [[Washington, D.C.]] to single mother Marquet Craig, then 14 years old. She supported her family by working as a [[cable television|cable TV]] installer for [[Comcast]], and moved the family nine times.<ref name=Underdog>{{cite news|url=http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2009/jul/08/underdog-bites-back-young-ready-to-top-for-griz/ |title=Underdog bites back: Sam Young ready to top expectations for Grizzlies  |first=Scott |last=Cacciola |newspaper=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |date=2009-07-08 |access-date=2009-07-08}}</ref> By the time Young was in high school, the family had found its way to [[Prince George's County, Maryland]]. At [[Friendly High School]] in [[Fort Washington, Maryland|Fort Washington]], Young led the Patriots to [[Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association|Maryland state titles]] in 2003 and 2004, averaging 24.6 points, 14.0 rebounds, and six blocked shots per game as a senior.<ref name="Pitt bio">{{cite web |url=http://pittsburghpanthers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/young_sam00.html |title=Men's Basketball, 2008–09 Roster: 23 Sam Young |publisher=University of Pittsburgh Athletic Department |access-date=2009-07-08 |archive-date=2009-03-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090308125815/http://pittsburghpanthers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/young_sam00.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

After graduating from high school, Young attended [[Hargrave Military Academy]] for a year as his high school grades meant that he would have to spend a year at a prep school in order to qualify for a [[athletic scholarship|scholarship]]. He averaged 23 points and 11 rebounds for a team that went 28–1 and was ranked second nationally among prep school programs. The basketball recruiting site ''Scout.com'' named Young its National Prep School Player of the Year for 2005. He also received the recruiting attention he had largely missed out on in high school, receiving offers from programs such as [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia]], [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], and [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]].<ref name="Pitt bio"/> He would decide to [[National Letter of Intent|sign]] with Pitt; Joe Lombardi,<!--Not to be confused with the football coach of the same name.--> then a Pitt assistant and now head coach at [[Indiana University of Pennsylvania]], speculated that Young chose Pitt because "[w]e were there when a whole lot of other people weren't around. He just wanted someone to give him some love."<ref name=Underdog/>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Young was listed as the No. 17 small forward and the No. 71 player in the nation in 2005.<ref>[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Sam-Young-12354;_ylt=Av2jKf94jALo7zhIeovlPQHXO5B4 Sam Young Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
Young joined the Pitt basketball team for the 2005–2006 season.<ref name="Pitt bio"/> He initially chafed at his role on the team; he wanted to display his perimeter skills, but head coach [[Jamie Dixon]] wanted him to play on the inside. Young nearly transferred to [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] after his sophomore year of 2006–07, but when the Wildcats' coach [[Bob Huggins]] left for [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] after that season, Dixon convinced Young to stay, indicating that he would have a much bigger role on the team in the upcoming season.<ref name=Underdog/> Dixon's prediction was borne out that season; Young averaged 18 points per game, was named the [[2008 Big East men's basketball tournament|2008 Big East tournament]] MVP after scoring 80 points in the tournament,<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/bigeast/pittsburgh.htm | work=USA Today | title=Pittsburgh - Team Notes | date=2010-04-06 | access-date=2010-05-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?columnist=glockner_andy&id=3439704|title=Glockner: Seniors to rule college hoops in 2008-09|date=June 20, 2008|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> and was also named the conference's [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player|most improved player]].<ref name=Bennett>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/ncaatourney09/news/story?id=4015385 |title=Work ethic takes Young to higher level |first=Brian |last=Bennett |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=2009-03-26 |access-date=2009-07-08}}</ref>

In his senior season at Pitt, Young averaged 19.2 points per game, and was given the honor of being a Third Team All-America. His 2009 NBA draft stock also increased after his spectacular performance in the 2009 NCAA Tournament in which he averaged 23.5 points in four games.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=4027698|title=Unanimous: OU's Griffin heads All-America list|date=March 30, 2009|website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nbadraft.net/2009mock_draft |title=2009 Mock Draft |access-date=2009-03-31 |archive-date=2012-09-06 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120906205306/http://www.nbadraft.net/2009mock_draft |url-status=dead }}</ref> He also received accolades from his opposition; [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]] coach [[Jim Calhoun]], who saw Young score 56 points in two games against [[2008–09 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|his team]] in Young's senior season, including 31 on Pitt's 2009 Senior Day, said, "There hasn't ever been a player who gives us as many problems as he does."<ref name=Bennett/>

==The Basketball Tournament==
Sam Young played for Team ATL AllStars in the [[The Basketball Tournament 2018|2018]] edition of [[The Basketball Tournament]]. He had a team-high 29 points and nine rebounds in the team's first-round loss to Louisiana United.

==Professional career==
Young was drafted by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] with the 36th overall pick in the [[2009 NBA draft]].

On March 15, 2012, Young was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for the rights to [[Ricky Sánchez]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers_acquire_sam_young_from__2012_03_15.html | title=SIXERS ACQUIRE SAM YOUNG FROM MEMPHIS - 3/15/2012 | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=March 15, 2012 | access-date=March 15, 2012}}</ref>

On September 6, 2012, Young signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-blake-ahearn-sam-young-sundiata-gaines|title=Pacers Sign Blake Ahearn, Sam Young, Sundiata Gaines|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> On January 6, 2013, he was waived by the Pacers<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/sam-young-released|title=Pacers Waive Young|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> but was later re-signed on January 28, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-re-sign-sam-young|title=Pacers Re-Sign Sam Young|website=www.nba.com}}</ref>

On September 30, 2013, Young signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/130930_spurs_training_camp_roster|title=Spurs Announce Training Camp Roster|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Spurs on October 10, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/131010_spurs_waive_sam_young|title=Spurs Waive Sam Young|website=www.nba.com}}</ref>

On November 18, 2013, Young signed with the Sydney Kings for the rest of the [[2013–14 NBL season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sydneykings.com/article/id/3d76ktm00iv71lsysswza6xjp|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131122045000/http://www.sydneykings.com/article/id/3d76ktm00iv71lsysswza6xjp|url-status=dead|title=Slam Young to give fans something to talk about|archivedate=November 22, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/article/id/71zwmk3bovtr1ai2153xi3a3h|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131120173112/http://www.nbl.com.au/article/id/71zwmk3bovtr1ai2153xi3a3h|url-status=dead|title=Introducing 'Slammin' Sam Young to the NBL|archivedate=November 20, 2013}}</ref> On February 4, 2014, Young was named the Player of the Month for January.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/article/id/1mbpjoaiyf3hp1twu7fjukw2pw|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140306082558/http://www.nbl.com.au/article/id/1mbpjoaiyf3hp1twu7fjukw2pw|url-status=dead|title=Young, Heal win Player and Coach of the Month|archivedate=March 6, 2014}}</ref> In 21 games for the Kings, Young averaged 21.9 points, 5.5 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.0 steals per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://websites.mygameday.app/team_info.cgi?pID=197266119|title=Sam Young - Player Statistics|website=GameDay}}</ref>

On January 19, 2014, Young signed with [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]] of Puerto Rico for the 2014 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cat/america/110549/sam-young-signs-with-vaqueros-de-bayamon.html|title=Sam Young signs with Vaqueros de Bayamon |work=Sportando }}</ref>

On July 22, 2014, he signed a one-year deal with [[Juvecaserta Basket]] of Italy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/128432/pasta-reggia-caserta-announces-former-nba-sam-young.html|title=Pasta Reggia Caserta announces former NBA Sam Young |work=Sportando }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.juvecaserta.it/firmato-sam-young/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140728223109/http://www.juvecaserta.it/firmato-sam-young/|url-status=dead|title=FIRMATO SAM YOUNG|archivedate=July 28, 2014}}</ref> On December 31, 2014, he parted ways with Juvecaserta.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/146882/sam-young-leaves-pasta-reggia-caserta.html|title=Sam Young leaves Pasta Reggia Caserta |work=Sportando }}</ref>

On January 14, 2015, he signed with Mexican team [[Halcones de Xalapa]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/148607/halcones-de-xalapa-land-former-nba-player-sam-young.html|title=Halcones de Xalapa land former NBA player Sam Young |work=Sportando }}</ref> On April 8, he signed with [[Muratbey Uşak Sportif]] of the [[Turkish Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/157734/sam-young-moves-to-usak-sportif.html|title=Sam Young moves to Usak Sportif |work=Sportando }}</ref>

On September 21, 2017, Young signed with [[Homenetmen Beirut B.C.|Homenetmen Beirut]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/asia/lebanon/247613/sam-young-inks-with-homenetmen.html|title=Sam Young inks with Homenetmen |work=Sportando }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Scott Cacciola of ''[[The Commercial Appeal]]'', the daily newspaper of the Grizzlies' home city of [[Memphis, Tennessee]], wrote:

{{quote|Young has long been known for his work ethic and his determination. At 6-6 and 210 pounds, he plays basketball in a minor key, all angst and controlled rage, motivated by those who had underestimated him, written him off, ignored him.<ref name=Underdog/>}}

Young's work ethic borders on the obsessive. While at Pitt, he practiced so much on his own that the coaching staff worried about his knees, and he would regularly play pick-up games at lunchtime during the season. During the summer before his senior year at Pitt, he went so far as to live for a month in a locker room at Pitt's home arena, the [[Petersen Events Center]], sleeping on an air mattress he had carried to the locker room, so he could work out and practice whenever he chose. Young himself admitted that basketball was his "love" and his girlfriend was his "mistress", adding, "And she knows that."<ref name=Underdog/>

One of Young's closest friends, former high school teammate and later [[University of South Florida|South Florida]] player Chris Howard, noted that Young's work ethic was present long before he came to Pitt:

{{quote|This is a guy who'd be at school at 6:30 in the morning working out or at the gym. When he was at Hargrave, there'd be times we'd call each other and be on speakerphone while we were doing push-ups. He's not one of those guys you're going to see in the [[nightclub|club]]. Sometimes he'll call me and say he's going to movies, and I'll joke around and say, 'Who are you going with? Who's the girl?' And he'll say, 'I'm going by myself.' That's the kind of focus you've got to have until you get to the place you want to be.<ref name=Bennett/>}}

He also found inspiration in his family. During his year at Hargrave, he put a poster in his dorm room that read "I can't let my mother work harder than I do." He also drew from his brother Michael Spriggs, who was born with [[cataract]]s and [[glaucoma]] and completely [[blindness|lost his sight]] at age 13,<ref name=Underdog/> but nonetheless reached the state championships in [[scholastic wrestling|high school wrestling]] and won a gold medal in [[judo]] at an international blind sports competition.<ref name=Bennett/> Young said about his brother, "It could have been me. And I know if he had my opportunities, he'd be doing something constructive with them."<ref name=Underdog/>

Young's athleticism is not limited to basketball. Before his senior year at Friendly High, he promised to do backflips if the Patriots won the state title, and proceeded to do exactly that.<ref name="Pitt bio"/> He also reportedly stunned Pitt's [[Diving (sport)|diving]] coach one day by climbing up to the 7½-meter board and performing a nearly perfect 2½ somersault into the pool.<ref name=Bennett/>

He also writes [[poetry]]; he has spoken with a publisher about compiling his works, and read some of his poems at an open-mic night at a Pittsburgh coffeehouse in 2008. He is also a skilled piano player.<ref name=Bennett/>
